question.text: Circuit breakers in the derivatives market are triggered when:

answer.text: The index moves beyond specified percentage thresholds (10%, 15%, 20%) from the previous day's closing value
Any single stock moves by more than 5%
Trading volume exceeds the daily average by 50%
The number of new client registrations exceeds 1,000 in a day

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI's market-wide circuit breaker framework, index-level circuit breakers are triggered when the benchmark index moves beyond specified percentage thresholds — typically 10%, 15% and 20% — measured against the previous day's closing value. When triggered, trading is halted across cash and derivatives segments for prescribed durations, with the length and timing of the halt depending on which threshold is breached and when during the trading day it occurs. The Trap: Single-stock moves trigger stock-specific price bands or operating ranges, not the market-wide circuit breaker. Volume spikes or client-registration counts are not the trigger; the index-level percentage move is. Note: The specific 10/15/20 percent index-circuit-breaker thresholds are not stated in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages — those pages discuss contract-level price bands and operating ranges. The framing above reflects general SEBI market-wide circuit-breaker rules rather than a workbook citation.
